Predict the human participant's choice in this anonymous, financially incentivized laboratory group interaction. The same 7,8 or 9 people interact for four regular rounds, then an extra round. Personal numbers remain fixed. No communication is allowed. In regular rounds Persons 1..4 (groups 7/8) or 1..5 (group 9) each receive EUR 2 and choose an amount 0..2 to allocate to a group project, keeping the rest. All members, including the other members initially endowed with 0, receive 0.30 times total allocations. Everyone then sees individual allocations and first-phase incomes. Only the initially zero-endowed members may reduce the contributors' incomes, using at most their own income from this phase. Each EUR 1 of own cost deducts EUR 3 from the selected contributor. These members cannot deduct from each other. The page first asks whether to make deductions, then, after yes, requests one simultaneous joint vector across 4 or 5 contributors. The money budget is checked at currency precision; preserve the recorded numeric precision, including fractional cents. After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. The extra round is announced, but its rules are explained only after the four regular rounds. Any prior private ratings supplied are your own already completed reports. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here. Original age and pre-laboratory self-report items, when provided, describe your own background; item wording is retained in English and rated 1=does not apply at all to 6=applies completely. Previously supplied own ratings use 1=do not agree at all to 6=agree completely. Missing records do not mean the human did not know their own information. Predict only the current requested action; no explanations.
Current action: you are on the joint deduction-cost entry page after choosing yes to its preceding question. Output a text JSON object with exactly the specified P 1..P 4 orP 5 fields, each a nonnegative own COST in EUR. The total cost rounded to currency precision must not exceed the available income.

These members cannot deduct from each other. The page first asks whether to make deductions, then, after yes, requests one simultaneous joint vector across 4 or 5 contributors. The money budget is checked at currency precision; preserve the recorded numeric precision, including fractional cents. After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. The extra round is announced, but its rules are explained only after the four regular rounds. Any prior private ratings supplied are your own already completed reports. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here. Personal numbers remain fixed. No communication is allowed. In regular rounds Persons 1..4 (groups 7/8) or 1..5 (group 9) each receive EUR 2 and choose an amount 0..2 to allocate to a group project, keeping the rest. All members, including the other members initially endowed with 0, receive 0.30 times total allocations. Everyone then sees individual allocations and first-phase incomes. Only the initially zero-endowed members may reduce the contributors' incomes, using at most their own income from this phase. Each EUR 1 of own cost deducts EUR 3 from the selected contributor. These members cannot deduct from each other. The page first asks whether to make deductions, then, after yes, requests one simultaneous joint vector across 4 or 5 contributors. The money budget is checked at currency precision; preserve the recorded numeric precision, including fractional cents. After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. The extra round is announced, but its rules are explained only after the four regular rounds. Any prior private ratings supplied are your own already completed reports. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here. Original age and pre-laboratory self-report items, when provided, describe your own background; item wording is retained in English and rated 1=does not apply at all to 6=applies completely. Previously supplied own ratings use 1=do not agree at all to 6=agree completely. Missing records do not mean the human did not know their own information. Predict only the current requested action; no explanations.
After rounds 1 and 4, people privately rate the others. After round 4 each privately submits one full ranking of all others, with rank 1 the most preferred person for reallocating up to EUR 5 after the extra round's first phase; no self-vote or repeated person is permitted. Instructions announce selection by best average rank and random tie breaking. In the extra round all people receive EUR 2 and simultaneously choose contributions 0..2, with each member receiving 0.15 times the total. Only subsequently does the chosen person reallocate up to EUR 5, conserving the total amount and possibly including themselves. The allocator identity is not shown on the contribution page.

All members, including the other members initially endowed with 0, receive 0.30 times total allocations. Everyone then sees individual allocations and first-phase incomes. Only the initially zero-endowed members may reduce the contributors' incomes, using at most their own income from this phase. Each EUR 1 of own cost deducts EUR 3 from the selected contributor. These members cannot deduct from each other. The page first asks whether to make deductions, then, after yes, requests one simultaneous joint vector across 4 or 5 contributors. The money budget is checked at currency precision; preserve the recorded numeric precision, including fractional cents. After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. The extra round is announced, but its rules are explained only after the four regular rounds. Any prior private ratings supplied are your own already completed reports. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Original age and pre-laboratory self-report items, when provided, describe your own background; item wording is retained in English and rated 1=does not apply at all to 6=applies completely. Previously supplied own ratings use 1=do not agree at all to 6=agree completely. Missing records do not mean the human did not know their own information. Predict only the current requested action; no explanations.

Instructions announce selection by best average rank and random tie breaking. In the extra round all people receive EUR 2 and simultaneously choose contributions 0..2, with each member receiving 0.15 times the total. Only the initially zero-endowed members may reduce the contributors' incomes, using at most their own income from this phase. Each EUR 1 of own cost deducts EUR 3 from the selected contributor. These members cannot deduct from each other. The page first asks whether to make deductions, then, after yes, requests one simultaneous joint vector across 4 or 5 contributors. The money budget is checked at currency precision; preserve the recorded numeric precision, including fractional cents. After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. The extra round is announced, but its rules are explained only after the four regular rounds. Any prior private ratings supplied are your own already completed reports. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here. Original age and pre-laboratory self-report items, when provided, describe your own background; item wording is retained in English and rated 1=does not apply at all to 6=applies completely. Previously supplied own ratings use 1=do not agree at all to 6=agree completely. Missing records do not mean the human did not know their own information. Predict only the current requested action; no explanations.
After rounds 1 and 4, people privately rate the others. After round 4 each privately submits one full ranking of all others, with rank 1 the most preferred person for reallocating up to EUR 5 after the extra round's first phase; no self-vote or repeated person is permitted. Instructions announce selection by best average rank and random tie breaking. In the extra round all people receive EUR 2 and simultaneously choose contributions 0..2, with each member receiving 0.15 times the total. Only subsequently does the chosen person reallocate up to EUR 5, conserving the total amount and possibly including themselves. The allocator identity is not shown on the contribution page.

These members cannot deduct from each other. The page first asks whether to make deductions, then, after yes, requests one simultaneous joint vector across 4 or 5 contributors. The money budget is checked at currency precision; preserve the recorded numeric precision, including fractional cents. After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. The extra round is announced, but its rules are explained only after the four regular rounds. Any prior private ratings supplied are your own already completed reports. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here. All members, including the other members initially endowed with 0, receive 0.30 times total allocations. Everyone then sees individual allocations and first-phase incomes. Only the initially zero-endowed members may reduce the contributors' incomes, using at most their own income from this phase. Each EUR 1 of own cost deducts EUR 3 from the selected contributor. These members cannot deduct from each other. The page first asks whether to make deductions, then, after yes, requests one simultaneous joint vector across 4 or 5 contributors. The money budget is checked at currency precision; preserve the recorded numeric precision, including fractional cents. After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. The extra round is announced, but its rules are explained only after the four regular rounds. Any prior private ratings supplied are your own already completed reports. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here. Original age and pre-laboratory self-report items, when provided, describe your own background; item wording is retained in English and rated 1=does not apply at all to 6=applies completely. Previously supplied own ratings use 1=do not agree at all to 6=agree completely. Missing records do not mean the human did not know their own information. Predict only the current requested action; no explanations.
After rounds 1 and 4, people privately rate the others. After round 4 each privately submits one full ranking of all others, with rank 1 the most preferred person for reallocating up to EUR 5 after the extra round's first phase; no self-vote or repeated person is permitted. Instructions announce selection by best average rank and random tie breaking. In the extra round all people receive EUR 2 and simultaneously choose contributions 0..2, with each member receiving 0.15 times the total. Only subsequently does the chosen person reallocate up to EUR 5, conserving the total amount and possibly including themselves. The allocator identity is not shown on the contribution page.

Predict the human participant's choice in this anonymous, financially incentivized laboratory group interaction. The same 7,8 or 9 people interact for four regular rounds, then an extra round. Personal numbers remain fixed. No communication is allowed. In regular rounds Persons 1..4 (groups 7/8) or 1..5 (group 9) each receive EUR 2 and choose an amount 0..2 to allocate to a group project, keeping the rest. All members, including the other members initially endowed with 0, receive 0.30 times total allocations. Everyone then sees individual allocations and first-phase incomes. Only the initially zero-endowed members may reduce the contributors' incomes, using at most their own income from this phase. Each EUR 1 of own cost deducts EUR 3 from the selected contributor. These members cannot deduct from each other. The page first asks whether to make deductions, then, after yes, requests one simultaneous joint vector across 4 or 5 contributors. The money budget is checked at currency precision; preserve the recorded numeric precision, including fractional cents. After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. The extra round is announced, but its rules are explained only after the four regular rounds. Any prior private ratings supplied are your own already completed reports. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here. Original age and pre-laboratory self-report items, when provided, describe your own background; item wording is retained in English and rated 1=does not apply at all to 6=applies completely. Previously supplied own ratings use 1=do not agree at all to 6=agree completely. Missing records do not mean the human did not know their own information. Predict only the current requested action; no explanations.
After rounds 1 and 4, people privately rate the others. After round 4 each privately submits one full ranking of all others, with rank 1 the most preferred person for reallocating up to EUR 5 after the extra round's first phase; no self-vote or repeated person is permitted. Instructions announce selection by best average rank and random tie breaking. In the extra round all people receive EUR 2 and simultaneously choose contributions 0..2, with each member receiving 0.15 times the total. Only subsequently does the chosen person reallocate up to EUR 5, conserving the total amount and possibly including themselves. The allocator identity is not shown on the contribution page. 
Current action: contribute to the extra-round project, now with all members able to contribute. Output only a number in EUR between 0 and 2. Your own previously submitted ballot is known to you; other individual ballots and the later allocation are absent.

After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. The extra round is announced, but its rules are explained only after the four regular rounds. Any prior private ratings supplied are your own already completed reports. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here. Predict the human participant's choice in this anonymous, financially incentivized laboratory group interaction. The same 7,8 or 9 people interact for four regular rounds, then an extra round. Personal numbers remain fixed. No communication is allowed. In regular rounds Persons 1..4 (groups 7/8) or 1..5 (group 9) each receive EUR 2 and choose an amount 0..2 to allocate to a group project, keeping the rest. All members, including the other members initially endowed with 0, receive 0.30 times total allocations. Everyone then sees individual allocations and first-phase incomes. Only the initially zero-endowed members may reduce the contributors' incomes, using at most their own income from this phase. Each EUR 1 of own cost deducts EUR 3 from the selected contributor. These members cannot deduct from each other. The page first asks whether to make deductions, then, after yes, requests one simultaneous joint vector across 4 or 5 contributors. The money budget is checked at currency precision; preserve the recorded numeric precision, including fractional cents. After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. The extra round is announced, but its rules are explained only after the four regular rounds. Any prior private ratings supplied are your own already completed reports. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here. Original age and pre-laboratory self-report items, when provided, describe your own background; item wording is retained in English and rated 1=does not apply at all to 6=applies completely. Previously supplied own ratings use 1=do not agree at all to 6=agree completely. Missing records do not mean the human did not know their own information. Predict only the current requested action; no explanations.
After rounds 1 and 4, people privately rate the others. After round 4 each privately submits one full ranking of all others, with rank 1 the most preferred person for reallocating up to EUR 5 after the extra round's first phase; no self-vote or repeated person is permitted. Instructions announce selection by best average rank and random tie breaking. In the extra round all people receive EUR 2 and simultaneously choose contributions 0..2, with each member receiving 0.15 times the total. Only subsequently does the chosen person reallocate up to EUR 5, conserving the total amount and possibly including themselves. The allocator identity is not shown on the contribution page. 
Current action: contribute to the extra-round project, now with all members able to contribute. Output only a number in EUR between 0 and 2. Your own previously submitted ballot is known to you; other individual ballots and the later allocation are absent.

The money budget is checked at currency precision; preserve the recorded numeric precision, including fractional cents. After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. The extra round is announced, but its rules are explained only after the four regular rounds. Any prior private ratings supplied are your own already completed reports. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here. After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here. Predict the human participant's choice in this anonymous, financially incentivized laboratory group interaction. The same 7,8 or 9 people interact for four regular rounds, then an extra round. Personal numbers remain fixed. No communication is allowed. In regular rounds Persons 1..4 (groups 7/8) or 1..5 (group 9) each receive EUR 2 and choose an amount 0..2 to allocate to a group project, keeping the rest. All members, including the other members initially endowed with 0, receive 0.30 times total allocations. Everyone then sees individual allocations and first-phase incomes. Only the initially zero-endowed members may reduce the contributors' incomes, using at most their own income from this phase. Each EUR 1 of own cost deducts EUR 3 from the selected contributor. These members cannot deduct from each other. The page first asks whether to make deductions, then, after yes, requests one simultaneous joint vector across 4 or 5 contributors. The money budget is checked at currency precision; preserve the recorded numeric precision, including fractional cents. After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. The extra round is announced, but its rules are explained only after the four regular rounds. Any prior private ratings supplied are your own already completed reports. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here. Original age and pre-laboratory self-report items, when provided, describe your own background; item wording is retained in English and rated 1=does not apply at all to 6=applies completely. Previously supplied own ratings use 1=do not agree at all to 6=agree completely. Missing records do not mean the human did not know their own information. Predict only the current requested action; no explanations.
After rounds 1 and 4, people privately rate the others. After round 4 each privately submits one full ranking of all others, with rank 1 the most preferred person for reallocating up to EUR 5 after the extra round's first phase; no self-vote or repeated person is permitted. Instructions announce selection by best average rank and random tie breaking. In the extra round all people receive EUR 2 and simultaneously choose contributions 0..2, with each member receiving 0.15 times the total. Only subsequently does the chosen person reallocate up to EUR 5, conserving the total amount and possibly including themselves. The allocator identity is not shown on the contribution page. 
Current action: contribute to the extra-round project, now with all members able to contribute. Output only a number in EUR between 0 and 2. Your own previously submitted ballot is known to you; other individual ballots and the later allocation are absent.

Personal numbers remain fixed. No communication is allowed. In regular rounds Persons 1..4 (groups 7/8) or 1..5 (group 9) each receive EUR 2 and choose an amount 0..2 to allocate to a group project, keeping the rest. All members, including the other members initially endowed with 0, receive 0.30 times total allocations. Everyone then sees individual allocations and first-phase incomes. Only the initially zero-endowed members may reduce the contributors' incomes, using at most their own income from this phase. Each EUR 1 of own cost deducts EUR 3 from the selected contributor. These members cannot deduct from each other. The page first asks whether to make deductions, then, after yes, requests one simultaneous joint vector across 4 or 5 contributors. The money budget is checked at currency precision; preserve the recorded numeric precision, including fractional cents. After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. The extra round is announced, but its rules are explained only after the four regular rounds. Any prior private ratings supplied are your own already completed reports. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here. Original age and pre-laboratory self-report items, when provided, describe your own background; item wording is retained in English and rated 1=does not apply at all to 6=applies completely. Previously supplied own ratings use 1=do not agree at all to 6=agree completely. Missing records do not mean the human did not know their own information. Predict only the current requested action; no explanations.
After rounds 1 and 4, people privately rate the others. After round 4 each privately submits one full ranking of all others, with rank 1 the most preferred person for reallocating up to EUR 5 after the extra round's first phase; no self-vote or repeated person is permitted. Instructions announce selection by best average rank and random tie breaking. In the extra round all people receive EUR 2 and simultaneously choose contributions 0..2, with each member receiving 0.15 times the total. Only subsequently does the chosen person reallocate up to EUR 5, conserving the total amount and possibly including themselves. The allocator identity is not shown on the contribution page.

Personal numbers remain fixed. No communication is allowed. In regular rounds Persons 1..4 (groups 7/8) or 1..5 (group 9) each receive EUR 2 and choose an amount 0..2 to allocate to a group project, keeping the rest. All members, including the other members initially endowed with 0, receive 0.30 times total allocations. Everyone then sees individual allocations and first-phase incomes. Only the initially zero-endowed members may reduce the contributors' incomes, using at most their own income from this phase. Each EUR 1 of own cost deducts EUR 3 from the selected contributor. These members cannot deduct from each other. The page first asks whether to make deductions, then, after yes, requests one simultaneous joint vector across 4 or 5 contributors. The money budget is checked at currency precision; preserve the recorded numeric precision, including fractional cents. After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. The extra round is announced, but its rules are explained only after the four regular rounds. Any prior private ratings supplied are your own already completed reports. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here. Original age and pre-laboratory self-report items, when provided, describe your own background; item wording is retained in English and rated 1=does not apply at all to 6=applies completely. Previously supplied own ratings use 1=do not agree at all to 6=agree completely. Missing records do not mean the human did not know their own information. Predict only the current requested action; no explanations.
After rounds 1 and 4, people privately rate the others. After round 4 each privately submits one full ranking of all others, with rank 1 the most preferred person for reallocating up to EUR 5 after the extra round's first phase; no self-vote or repeated person is permitted. Instructions announce selection by best average rank and random tie breaking. In the extra round all people receive EUR 2 and simultaneously choose contributions 0..2, with each member receiving 0.15 times the total. Only subsequently does the chosen person reallocate up to EUR 5, conserving the total amount and possibly including themselves. The allocator identity is not shown on the contribution page.

All members, including the other members initially endowed with 0, receive 0.30 times total allocations. Everyone then sees individual allocations and first-phase incomes. Only the initially zero-endowed members may reduce the contributors' incomes, using at most their own income from this phase. Each EUR 1 of own cost deducts EUR 3 from the selected contributor. These members cannot deduct from each other. The page first asks whether to make deductions, then, after yes, requests one simultaneous joint vector across 4 or 5 contributors. The money budget is checked at currency precision; preserve the recorded numeric precision, including fractional cents. After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. The extra round is announced, but its rules are explained only after the four regular rounds. Any prior private ratings supplied are your own already completed reports. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here. Original age and pre-laboratory self-report items, when provided, describe your own background; item wording is retained in English and rated 1=does not apply at all to 6=applies completely. Previously supplied own ratings use 1=do not agree at all to 6=agree completely. Missing records do not mean the human did not know their own information. Predict only the current requested action; no explanations.

All members, including the other members initially endowed with 0, receive 0.30 times total allocations. Everyone then sees individual allocations and first-phase incomes. Only the initially zero-endowed members may reduce the contributors' incomes, using at most their own income from this phase. Each EUR 1 of own cost deducts EUR 3 from the selected contributor. These members cannot deduct from each other. The page first asks whether to make deductions, then, after yes, requests one simultaneous joint vector across 4 or 5 contributors. The money budget is checked at currency precision; preserve the recorded numeric precision, including fractional cents. After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. The extra round is announced, but its rules are explained only after the four regular rounds. Any prior private ratings supplied are your own already completed reports. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here. Original age and pre-laboratory self-report items, when provided, describe your own background; item wording is retained in English and rated 1=does not apply at all to 6=applies completely. Previously supplied own ratings use 1=do not agree at all to 6=agree completely. Missing records do not mean the human did not know their own information. Predict only the current requested action; no explanations.

Personal numbers remain fixed. No communication is allowed. In regular rounds Persons 1..4 (groups 7/8) or 1..5 (group 9) each receive EUR 2 and choose an amount 0..2 to allocate to a group project, keeping the rest. All members, including the other members initially endowed with 0, receive 0.30 times total allocations. Everyone then sees individual allocations and first-phase incomes. Only the initially zero-endowed members may reduce the contributors' incomes, using at most their own income from this phase. Each EUR 1 of own cost deducts EUR 3 from the selected contributor. These members cannot deduct from each other. The page first asks whether to make deductions, then, after yes, requests one simultaneous joint vector across 4 or 5 contributors. The money budget is checked at currency precision; preserve the recorded numeric precision, including fractional cents. After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. The extra round is announced, but its rules are explained only after the four regular rounds. Any prior private ratings supplied are your own already completed reports. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here. Original age and pre-laboratory self-report items, when provided, describe your own background; item wording is retained in English and rated 1=does not apply at all to 6=applies completely. Previously supplied own ratings use 1=do not agree at all to 6=agree completely. Missing records do not mean the human did not know their own information. Predict only the current requested action; no explanations.

In regular rounds Persons 1..4 (groups 7/8) or 1..5 (group 9) each receive EUR 2 and choose an amount 0..2 to allocate to a group project, keeping the rest. All members, including the other members initially endowed with 0, receive 0.30 times total allocations. Everyone then sees individual allocations and first-phase incomes. Only the initially zero-endowed members may reduce the contributors' incomes, using at most their own income from this phase. Each EUR 1 of own cost deducts EUR 3 from the selected contributor. These members cannot deduct from each other. The page first asks whether to make deductions, then, after yes, requests one simultaneous joint vector across 4 or 5 contributors. The money budget is checked at currency precision; preserve the recorded numeric precision, including fractional cents. After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. The extra round is announced, but its rules are explained only after the four regular rounds. Any prior private ratings supplied are your own already completed reports. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here. Original age and pre-laboratory self-report items, when provided, describe your own background; item wording is retained in English and rated 1=does not apply at all to 6=applies completely. Previously supplied own ratings use 1=do not agree at all to 6=agree completely. Missing records do not mean the human did not know their own information. Predict only the current requested action; no explanations.

Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here. Personal numbers remain fixed. No communication is allowed. In regular rounds Persons 1..4 (groups 7/8) or 1..5 (group 9) each receive EUR 2 and choose an amount 0..2 to allocate to a group project, keeping the rest. All members, including the other members initially endowed with 0, receive 0.30 times total allocations. Everyone then sees individual allocations and first-phase incomes. Only the initially zero-endowed members may reduce the contributors' incomes, using at most their own income from this phase. Each EUR 1 of own cost deducts EUR 3 from the selected contributor. These members cannot deduct from each other. The page first asks whether to make deductions, then, after yes, requests one simultaneous joint vector across 4 or 5 contributors. The money budget is checked at currency precision; preserve the recorded numeric precision, including fractional cents. After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. The extra round is announced, but its rules are explained only after the four regular rounds. Any prior private ratings supplied are your own already completed reports. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here. Original age and pre-laboratory self-report items, when provided, describe your own background; item wording is retained in English and rated 1=does not apply at all to 6=applies completely. Previously supplied own ratings use 1=do not agree at all to 6=agree completely. Missing records do not mean the human did not know their own information. Predict only the current requested action; no explanations.
After rounds 1 and 4, people privately rate the others. After round 4 each privately submits one full ranking of all others, with rank 1 the most preferred person for reallocating up to EUR 5 after the extra round's first phase; no self-vote or repeated person is permitted. Instructions announce selection by best average rank and random tie breaking. In the extra round all people receive EUR 2 and simultaneously choose contributions 0..2, with each member receiving 0.15 times the total. Only subsequently does the chosen person reallocate up to EUR 5, conserving the total amount and possibly including themselves. The allocator identity is not shown on the contribution page.

Predict the human participant's choice in this anonymous, financially incentivized laboratory group interaction. The same 7,8 or 9 people interact for four regular rounds, then an extra round. Personal numbers remain fixed. No communication is allowed. In regular rounds Persons 1..4 (groups 7/8) or 1..5 (group 9) each receive EUR 2 and choose an amount 0..2 to allocate to a group project, keeping the rest. All members, including the other members initially endowed with 0, receive 0.30 times total allocations. Everyone then sees individual allocations and first-phase incomes. Only the initially zero-endowed members may reduce the contributors' incomes, using at most their own income from this phase. Each EUR 1 of own cost deducts EUR 3 from the selected contributor. These members cannot deduct from each other. The page first asks whether to make deductions, then, after yes, requests one simultaneous joint vector across 4 or 5 contributors. The money budget is checked at currency precision; preserve the recorded numeric precision, including fractional cents. After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. The extra round is announced, but its rules are explained only after the four regular rounds. Any prior private ratings supplied are your own already completed reports. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here. Original age and pre-laboratory self-report items, when provided, describe your own background; item wording is retained in English and rated 1=does not apply at all to 6=applies completely. Previously supplied own ratings use 1=do not agree at all to 6=agree completely. Missing records do not mean the human did not know their own information. Predict only the current requested action; no explanations.

Personal numbers remain fixed. No communication is allowed. In regular rounds Persons 1..4 (groups 7/8) or 1..5 (group 9) each receive EUR 2 and choose an amount 0..2 to allocate to a group project, keeping the rest. All members, including the other members initially endowed with 0, receive 0.30 times total allocations. Everyone then sees individual allocations and first-phase incomes. Only the initially zero-endowed members may reduce the contributors' incomes, using at most their own income from this phase. Each EUR 1 of own cost deducts EUR 3 from the selected contributor. These members cannot deduct from each other. The page first asks whether to make deductions, then, after yes, requests one simultaneous joint vector across 4 or 5 contributors. The money budget is checked at currency precision; preserve the recorded numeric precision, including fractional cents. After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. The extra round is announced, but its rules are explained only after the four regular rounds. Any prior private ratings supplied are your own already completed reports. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here. Original age and pre-laboratory self-report items, when provided, describe your own background; item wording is retained in English and rated 1=does not apply at all to 6=applies completely. Previously supplied own ratings use 1=do not agree at all to 6=agree completely. Missing records do not mean the human did not know their own information. Predict only the current requested action; no explanations.
After rounds 1 and 4, people privately rate the others. After round 4 each privately submits one full ranking of all others, with rank 1 the most preferred person for reallocating up to EUR 5 after the extra round's first phase; no self-vote or repeated person is permitted. Instructions announce selection by best average rank and random tie breaking. In the extra round all people receive EUR 2 and simultaneously choose contributions 0..2, with each member receiving 0.15 times the total. Only subsequently does the chosen person reallocate up to EUR 5, conserving the total amount and possibly including themselves. The allocator identity is not shown on the contribution page.

All members, including the other members initially endowed with 0, receive 0.30 times total allocations. Everyone then sees individual allocations and first-phase incomes. Only the initially zero-endowed members may reduce the contributors' incomes, using at most their own income from this phase. Each EUR 1 of own cost deducts EUR 3 from the selected contributor. These members cannot deduct from each other. The page first asks whether to make deductions, then, after yes, requests one simultaneous joint vector across 4 or 5 contributors. The money budget is checked at currency precision; preserve the recorded numeric precision, including fractional cents. After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. The extra round is announced, but its rules are explained only after the four regular rounds. Any prior private ratings supplied are your own already completed reports. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here. Original age and pre-laboratory self-report items, when provided, describe your own background; item wording is retained in English and rated 1=does not apply at all to 6=applies completely. Previously supplied own ratings use 1=do not agree at all to 6=agree completely. Missing records do not mean the human did not know their own information. Predict only the current requested action; no explanations.

Predict the human participant's choice in this anonymous, financially incentivized laboratory group interaction. The same 7,8 or 9 people interact for four regular rounds, then an extra round. Personal numbers remain fixed. No communication is allowed. In regular rounds Persons 1..4 (groups 7/8) or 1..5 (group 9) each receive EUR 2 and choose an amount 0..2 to allocate to a group project, keeping the rest. All members, including the other members initially endowed with 0, receive 0.30 times total allocations. Everyone then sees individual allocations and first-phase incomes. Only the initially zero-endowed members may reduce the contributors' incomes, using at most their own income from this phase. Each EUR 1 of own cost deducts EUR 3 from the selected contributor. These members cannot deduct from each other. The page first asks whether to make deductions, then, after yes, requests one simultaneous joint vector across 4 or 5 contributors. The money budget is checked at currency precision; preserve the recorded numeric precision, including fractional cents. After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. The extra round is announced, but its rules are explained only after the four regular rounds. Any prior private ratings supplied are your own already completed reports. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here. Original age and pre-laboratory self-report items, when provided, describe your own background; item wording is retained in English and rated 1=does not apply at all to 6=applies completely. Previously supplied own ratings use 1=do not agree at all to 6=agree completely. Missing records do not mean the human did not know their own information. Predict only the current requested action; no explanations.
Current action: allocate money to the regular-round group project. Output only a number in EUR between 0 and 2; the rest is kept privately.

Only the initially zero-endowed members may reduce the contributors' incomes, using at most their own income from this phase. Each EUR 1 of own cost deducts EUR 3 from the selected contributor. These members cannot deduct from each other. The page first asks whether to make deductions, then, after yes, requests one simultaneous joint vector across 4 or 5 contributors. The money budget is checked at currency precision; preserve the recorded numeric precision, including fractional cents. After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. The extra round is announced, but its rules are explained only after the four regular rounds. Any prior private ratings supplied are your own already completed reports. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here. Predict the human participant's choice in this anonymous, financially incentivized laboratory group interaction. The same 7,8 or 9 people interact for four regular rounds, then an extra round. Personal numbers remain fixed. No communication is allowed. In regular rounds Persons 1..4 (groups 7/8) or 1..5 (group 9) each receive EUR 2 and choose an amount 0..2 to allocate to a group project, keeping the rest. All members, including the other members initially endowed with 0, receive 0.30 times total allocations. Everyone then sees individual allocations and first-phase incomes. Only the initially zero-endowed members may reduce the contributors' incomes, using at most their own income from this phase. Each EUR 1 of own cost deducts EUR 3 from the selected contributor. These members cannot deduct from each other. The page first asks whether to make deductions, then, after yes, requests one simultaneous joint vector across 4 or 5 contributors. The money budget is checked at currency precision; preserve the recorded numeric precision, including fractional cents. After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. The extra round is announced, but its rules are explained only after the four regular rounds. Any prior private ratings supplied are your own already completed reports. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here. Original age and pre-laboratory self-report items, when provided, describe your own background; item wording is retained in English and rated 1=does not apply at all to 6=applies completely. Previously supplied own ratings use 1=do not agree at all to 6=agree completely. Missing records do not mean the human did not know their own information. Predict only the current requested action; no explanations.
After rounds 1 and 4, people privately rate the others. After round 4 each privately submits one full ranking of all others, with rank 1 the most preferred person for reallocating up to EUR 5 after the extra round's first phase; no self-vote or repeated person is permitted. Instructions announce selection by best average rank and random tie breaking. In the extra round all people receive EUR 2 and simultaneously choose contributions 0..2, with each member receiving 0.15 times the total. Only subsequently does the chosen person reallocate up to EUR 5, conserving the total amount and possibly including themselves. The allocator identity is not shown on the contribution page. 
Current action: contribute to the extra-round project, now with all members able to contribute. Output only a number in EUR between 0 and 2. Your own previously submitted ballot is known to you; other individual ballots and the later allocation are absent.

These members cannot deduct from each other. The page first asks whether to make deductions, then, after yes, requests one simultaneous joint vector across 4 or 5 contributors. The money budget is checked at currency precision; preserve the recorded numeric precision, including fractional cents. After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. The extra round is announced, but its rules are explained only after the four regular rounds. Any prior private ratings supplied are your own already completed reports. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here. Predict the human participant's choice in this anonymous, financially incentivized laboratory group interaction. The same 7,8 or 9 people interact for four regular rounds, then an extra round. Personal numbers remain fixed. No communication is allowed. In regular rounds Persons 1..4 (groups 7/8) or 1..5 (group 9) each receive EUR 2 and choose an amount 0..2 to allocate to a group project, keeping the rest. All members, including the other members initially endowed with 0, receive 0.30 times total allocations. Everyone then sees individual allocations and first-phase incomes. Only the initially zero-endowed members may reduce the contributors' incomes, using at most their own income from this phase. Each EUR 1 of own cost deducts EUR 3 from the selected contributor. These members cannot deduct from each other. The page first asks whether to make deductions, then, after yes, requests one simultaneous joint vector across 4 or 5 contributors. The money budget is checked at currency precision; preserve the recorded numeric precision, including fractional cents. After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. The extra round is announced, but its rules are explained only after the four regular rounds. Any prior private ratings supplied are your own already completed reports. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here. Original age and pre-laboratory self-report items, when provided, describe your own background; item wording is retained in English and rated 1=does not apply at all to 6=applies completely. Previously supplied own ratings use 1=do not agree at all to 6=agree completely. Missing records do not mean the human did not know their own information. Predict only the current requested action; no explanations.
After rounds 1 and 4, people privately rate the others. After round 4 each privately submits one full ranking of all others, with rank 1 the most preferred person for reallocating up to EUR 5 after the extra round's first phase; no self-vote or repeated person is permitted. Instructions announce selection by best average rank and random tie breaking. In the extra round all people receive EUR 2 and simultaneously choose contributions 0..2, with each member receiving 0.15 times the total. Only subsequently does the chosen person reallocate up to EUR 5, conserving the total amount and possibly including themselves. The allocator identity is not shown on the contribution page.

Personal numbers remain fixed. No communication is allowed. In regular rounds Persons 1..4 (groups 7/8) or 1..5 (group 9) each receive EUR 2 and choose an amount 0..2 to allocate to a group project, keeping the rest. All members, including the other members initially endowed with 0, receive 0.30 times total allocations. Everyone then sees individual allocations and first-phase incomes. Only the initially zero-endowed members may reduce the contributors' incomes, using at most their own income from this phase. Each EUR 1 of own cost deducts EUR 3 from the selected contributor. These members cannot deduct from each other. The page first asks whether to make deductions, then, after yes, requests one simultaneous joint vector across 4 or 5 contributors. The money budget is checked at currency precision; preserve the recorded numeric precision, including fractional cents. After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. The extra round is announced, but its rules are explained only after the four regular rounds. Any prior private ratings supplied are your own already completed reports. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here. Original age and pre-laboratory self-report items, when provided, describe your own background; item wording is retained in English and rated 1=does not apply at all to 6=applies completely. Previously supplied own ratings use 1=do not agree at all to 6=agree completely. Missing records do not mean the human did not know their own information. Predict only the current requested action; no explanations.
After rounds 1 and 4, people privately rate the others. After round 4 each privately submits one full ranking of all others, with rank 1 the most preferred person for reallocating up to EUR 5 after the extra round's first phase; no self-vote or repeated person is permitted. Instructions announce selection by best average rank and random tie breaking. In the extra round all people receive EUR 2 and simultaneously choose contributions 0..2, with each member receiving 0.15 times the total. Only subsequently does the chosen person reallocate up to EUR 5, conserving the total amount and possibly including themselves. The allocator identity is not shown on the contribution page.

Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Predict the human participant's choice in this anonymous, financially incentivized laboratory group interaction. The same 7,8 or 9 people interact for four regular rounds, then an extra round. Personal numbers remain fixed. No communication is allowed. In regular rounds Persons 1..4 (groups 7/8) or 1..5 (group 9) each receive EUR 2 and choose an amount 0..2 to allocate to a group project, keeping the rest. All members, including the other members initially endowed with 0, receive 0.30 times total allocations. Everyone then sees individual allocations and first-phase incomes. Only the initially zero-endowed members may reduce the contributors' incomes, using at most their own income from this phase. Each EUR 1 of own cost deducts EUR 3 from the selected contributor. These members cannot deduct from each other. The page first asks whether to make deductions, then, after yes, requests one simultaneous joint vector across 4 or 5 contributors. The money budget is checked at currency precision; preserve the recorded numeric precision, including fractional cents. After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. The extra round is announced, but its rules are explained only after the four regular rounds. Any prior private ratings supplied are your own already completed reports. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here. Original age and pre-laboratory self-report items, when provided, describe your own background; item wording is retained in English and rated 1=does not apply at all to 6=applies completely. Previously supplied own ratings use 1=do not agree at all to 6=agree completely. Missing records do not mean the human did not know their own information. Predict only the current requested action; no explanations.
Current action: allocate money to the regular-round group project. Output only a number in EUR between 0 and 2; the rest is kept privately.

Personal numbers remain fixed. No communication is allowed. In regular rounds Persons 1..4 (groups 7/8) or 1..5 (group 9) each receive EUR 2 and choose an amount 0..2 to allocate to a group project, keeping the rest. All members, including the other members initially endowed with 0, receive 0.30 times total allocations. Everyone then sees individual allocations and first-phase incomes. Only the initially zero-endowed members may reduce the contributors' incomes, using at most their own income from this phase. Each EUR 1 of own cost deducts EUR 3 from the selected contributor. These members cannot deduct from each other. The page first asks whether to make deductions, then, after yes, requests one simultaneous joint vector across 4 or 5 contributors. The money budget is checked at currency precision; preserve the recorded numeric precision, including fractional cents. After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. The extra round is announced, but its rules are explained only after the four regular rounds. Any prior private ratings supplied are your own already completed reports. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here. Original age and pre-laboratory self-report items, when provided, describe your own background; item wording is retained in English and rated 1=does not apply at all to 6=applies completely. Previously supplied own ratings use 1=do not agree at all to 6=agree completely. Missing records do not mean the human did not know their own information. Predict only the current requested action; no explanations.
After rounds 1 and 4, people privately rate the others. After round 4 each privately submits one full ranking of all others, with rank 1 the most preferred person for reallocating up to EUR 5 after the extra round's first phase; no self-vote or repeated person is permitted. Instructions announce selection by best average rank and random tie breaking. In the extra round all people receive EUR 2 and simultaneously choose contributions 0..2, with each member receiving 0.15 times the total. Only subsequently does the chosen person reallocate up to EUR 5, conserving the total amount and possibly including themselves. The allocator identity is not shown on the contribution page.

After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. The extra round is announced, but its rules are explained only after the four regular rounds. Any prior private ratings supplied are your own already completed reports. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here. Predict the human participant's choice in this anonymous, financially incentivized laboratory group interaction. The same 7,8 or 9 people interact for four regular rounds, then an extra round. Personal numbers remain fixed. No communication is allowed. In regular rounds Persons 1..4 (groups 7/8) or 1..5 (group 9) each receive EUR 2 and choose an amount 0..2 to allocate to a group project, keeping the rest. All members, including the other members initially endowed with 0, receive 0.30 times total allocations. Everyone then sees individual allocations and first-phase incomes. Only the initially zero-endowed members may reduce the contributors' incomes, using at most their own income from this phase. Each EUR 1 of own cost deducts EUR 3 from the selected contributor. These members cannot deduct from each other. The page first asks whether to make deductions, then, after yes, requests one simultaneous joint vector across 4 or 5 contributors. The money budget is checked at currency precision; preserve the recorded numeric precision, including fractional cents. After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. The extra round is announced, but its rules are explained only after the four regular rounds. Any prior private ratings supplied are your own already completed reports. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here. Original age and pre-laboratory self-report items, when provided, describe your own background; item wording is retained in English and rated 1=does not apply at all to 6=applies completely. Previously supplied own ratings use 1=do not agree at all to 6=agree completely. Missing records do not mean the human did not know their own information. Predict only the current requested action; no explanations.
After rounds 1 and 4, people privately rate the others. After round 4 each privately submits one full ranking of all others, with rank 1 the most preferred person for reallocating up to EUR 5 after the extra round's first phase; no self-vote or repeated person is permitted. Instructions announce selection by best average rank and random tie breaking. In the extra round all people receive EUR 2 and simultaneously choose contributions 0..2, with each member receiving 0.15 times the total. Only subsequently does the chosen person reallocate up to EUR 5, conserving the total amount and possibly including themselves. The allocator identity is not shown on the contribution page. 
Current action: contribute to the extra-round project, now with all members able to contribute. Output only a number in EUR between 0 and 2. Your own previously submitted ballot is known to you; other individual ballots and the later allocation are absent.

Predict the human participant's choice in this anonymous, financially incentivized laboratory group interaction. The same 7,8 or 9 people interact for four regular rounds, then an extra round. Personal numbers remain fixed. No communication is allowed. In regular rounds Persons 1..4 (groups 7/8) or 1..5 (group 9) each receive EUR 2 and choose an amount 0..2 to allocate to a group project, keeping the rest. All members, including the other members initially endowed with 0, receive 0.30 times total allocations. Everyone then sees individual allocations and first-phase incomes. Only the initially zero-endowed members may reduce the contributors' incomes, using at most their own income from this phase. Each EUR 1 of own cost deducts EUR 3 from the selected contributor. These members cannot deduct from each other. The page first asks whether to make deductions, then, after yes, requests one simultaneous joint vector across 4 or 5 contributors. The money budget is checked at currency precision; preserve the recorded numeric precision, including fractional cents. After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. The extra round is announced, but its rules are explained only after the four regular rounds. Any prior private ratings supplied are your own already completed reports. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here. Original age and pre-laboratory self-report items, when provided, describe your own background; item wording is retained in English and rated 1=does not apply at all to 6=applies completely. Previously supplied own ratings use 1=do not agree at all to 6=agree completely. Missing records do not mean the human did not know their own information. Predict only the current requested action; no explanations.
After rounds 1 and 4, people privately rate the others. After round 4 each privately submits one full ranking of all others, with rank 1 the most preferred person for reallocating up to EUR 5 after the extra round's first phase; no self-vote or repeated person is permitted. Instructions announce selection by best average rank and random tie breaking. In the extra round all people receive EUR 2 and simultaneously choose contributions 0..2, with each member receiving 0.15 times the total. Only subsequently does the chosen person reallocate up to EUR 5, conserving the total amount and possibly including themselves. The allocator identity is not shown on the contribution page. 
Current action: contribute to the extra-round project, now with all members able to contribute. Output only a number in EUR between 0 and 2. Your own previously submitted ballot is known to you; other individual ballots and the later allocation are absent.

In regular rounds Persons 1..4 (groups 7/8) or 1..5 (group 9) each receive EUR 2 and choose an amount 0..2 to allocate to a group project, keeping the rest. All members, including the other members initially endowed with 0, receive 0.30 times total allocations. Everyone then sees individual allocations and first-phase incomes. Only the initially zero-endowed members may reduce the contributors' incomes, using at most their own income from this phase. Each EUR 1 of own cost deducts EUR 3 from the selected contributor. These members cannot deduct from each other. The page first asks whether to make deductions, then, after yes, requests one simultaneous joint vector across 4 or 5 contributors. The money budget is checked at currency precision; preserve the recorded numeric precision, including fractional cents. After this phase everyone sees all allocations, individual deduction costs and resulting incomes. Each new regular round resets endowments. Do not impose a zero floor absent from the actual program. The extra round is announced, but its rules are explained only after the four regular rounds. Any prior private ratings supplied are your own already completed reports. Fixed remuneration of EUR 12 or study credits is additional; monetary earnings over paid rounds and earlier online tasks determine the variable payment. Two unpaid computer practice trials preceded the paid rounds. Exact individual practice/earlier online allocation responses are not reconstructed here.
